Σ 751
# Storybook parity

`packages/storybook/scripts/storybook-parity.mjs` measures the Storybook addon against Storybook's own docgen on real repositories: how often the addon hands a component on, what it documents that Storybook doesn't, where the two disagree, and what each costs. It is not run in CI; it needs the corpora `scripts/parity.py setup` fetches, installed, plus the native binding.

```bash
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook build
node packages/storybook/scripts/storybook-parity.mjs --corpora .corpora/repos --sample 120 --out report/storybook-parity
```

Output: `<out>.json` (every number) and `<out>.md` (tables). Storybook writes its cache into each corpus's `node_modules/.cache`, so the run needs write access there.

## What is compared

| Side | How it runs |
| --- | --- |
| Storybook's docgen | `@storybook/react`'s own `docgen-worker.js` (react-component-meta), unmodified, called as a middleware. It needs the TypeScript 5/6 compiler API, so `typescript` is redirected to `apps/oracle`'s TypeScript 6 (`--typescript` overrides); this package's TypeScript 7 has none. |
| The addon | `dist/provider.js`, the real `createDocgenProvider`, with Storybook's `meta.component` resolver and argTypes converter. |

Variants of the addon:

| Variant                | `loadDependencies` | `collapseInheritedProps` | `fallback`                           |
| ---------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `caliper`              | on                 | none                     | degraded (the addon's defaults)      |
| `caliper-nodeps`       | off                | none                     | degraded (what the addon did before) |
| `caliper-curated`      | on                 | dependencies             | degraded                             |
| `caliper-never`        | on                 | none                     | never                                |
| `caliper-nodeps-never` | off                | none                     | never                                |

The `-never` variants answer for every component whatever its diagnostics say. Comparing them shows the information the addon holds; comparing the others shows what the `degraded` rule lets through.

Two story sets per corpus:

- **Real stories**: the corpus's own `*.stories.*` files that name `component:` (Chakra: 1 of 125, Spectrum: 129 of 132; Mantine, shadcn and antd have none).
- **Sampled components**: one generated `export default { component }` story per sampled component (`--sample`), written beside the component and removed afterwards. Components that aren't a named or default export are skipped.

Per story, both sides' argTypes are reduced to control kind (`type.name`), options, required, type text, default and whether a description exists, then diffed prop by prop. **Extra props** are props only the addon lists. The report also has the session-level fallback rate: components whose extraction carries a warning or error, over all components, without any story.

Not measured: Storybook's control inference from argTypes (kind is `type.name`), and runtime behaviour in a real Storybook process (the worker thread, concurrency, caching). Timings include the first request, which starts the session; the TypeScript baseline's include building its program. Storybook with thousands of stories scales differently from these samples.

## Results

2026-10-24, main through #152 plus the addon options of #155, Apple silicon. Peak RSS is the child process's.

### Fallback rate: components the addon would hand on

| Corpus   | Components | nodeps | deps (default) | deps, curated |
| -------- | ---------- | ------ | -------------- | ------------- |
| Mantine  | 344        | 70.1%  | 68.6%          | 68.6%         |
| Chakra   | 609        | 55.9%  | **92.1%**      | 92.1%         |
| shadcn   | 1892       | 45.8%  | 42.1%          | 40.6%         |
| antd     | 248        | 42.3%  | 27.4%          | 27.0%         |
| Spectrum | 1647       | 38.4%  | 37.9%          | 37.9%         |

Session init: 47–91 ms without dependencies, 76–490 ms with; peak RSS 128–261 MB without, 157–786 MB with.

- **Loading dependencies lowers the rate except on Chakra**, where it rises from 56% to 92%: Chakra's style props pull csstype in, 557 components hit `Max resolution depth exceeded` and 561 get unresolved-reference warnings, and the session holds 470,957 props (773 per component) against 582 without dependencies. Without them those components answer with almost no props (the 34 sampled Chakra stories it answers miss 39,008 props Storybook lists), so the `degraded` rule is right to hand them on.
- `collapseInheritedProps: 'dependencies'` changes nothing on Chakra, Mantine and Spectrum and trims shadcn (13,244 → 7,682 props).
- The leading reasons are unresolved references to dependency types (Chakra, Spectrum, antd), `cannot be used as a component` and `Cannot find the component whose props are referenced` (shadcn).

### Against Storybook's docgen (sampled components; `caliper` = the defaults)

| Corpus (stories) | Storybook s / MB | caliper s / MB, answered | caliper-never s / MB | Extra props | Props only Storybook lists | Default only Storybook |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mantine (18) | 1.0 / 462 | 0.2 / 252, 14 | 0.2 / 249 | 0 | 8 in 4 stories | 0 |
| Chakra (102) | 4.0 / 1186 | 0.8 / 787, **10** | 1.3 / 844 | 9 | 993 in 13 | 39 |
| shadcn (112) | 3.3 / 1218 | 0.8 / 323, 68 | 0.8 / 326 | 446 (87 described) | 76 in 21 | 21 |
| antd (83) | 2.8 / 1051 | 0.4 / 238, 43 | 0.5 / 239 | 41 | 129 in 13 | 39 |
| Spectrum (102) | 2.6 / 1384 | 2.3 / 331, 63 | 1.9 / 328 | 1683 (576 described) | 7 in 6 | 48 |
| Spectrum real stories (129) | 1.3 / 686 | 2.8 / 340, 22 | 2.2 / 352 | 6530 (2390 described) | 0 | 0 |

- **Extra information.** What the addon lists and Storybook's docgen doesn't is inherited library props: DOM event handlers (`onPointerMoveCapture`), `aria-*`, Spectrum's style props (`UNSAFE_className`, `marginY`, `zIndex`), `isDisabled`/`isInvalid` from react-aria hooks. 38% of Spectrum's real-story extras and 20% of shadcn's carry a description. Whether that is more help or more noise in a controls panel is a product choice (`htmlAttributes`, `collapseInheritedProps`).
- **Cost.** The addon is 1.2–5× faster on these samples and uses 1.1–4× less memory (Chakra with dependencies is the exception: 844 MB against 1186 MB). The TypeScript baseline's time grows with the programs' size; the addon's first request pays the whole-corpus session.
- **Where the addon is behind.** Defaults Storybook reports and the addon doesn't (39–48 per corpus), 129 props in 13 antd stories, 993 in 13 Chakra stories, control kind differing on 60 of 917 shared antd props, and type text identical on only 60–70% of shared props (formatting included).
- **Reachability.** 20 antd and 114 of 129 real Spectrum stories name a component outside the configured `srcDirs` or a path the session can't match, which counts as handed on. Spectrum needed `starters` added to `srcDirs`.

## Reading the next run

The numbers to watch after the session work: the `caliper` degraded rate per corpus (target: below the `-never` gap), `Props only Storybook lists` (target 0), and the `caliper` seconds and MB columns for the first request.

593	      variants: { type: 'string' },

595	    },
596	  })

598	  const options = {
599	    corpora: resolve(values.corpora),
600	    limit: values.limit ? Number(values.limit) : Infinity,

614	        ? await runSession(values.variant, values.corpus, options)
615	        : await runStories(values.variant, values.corpus, options)
616	    process.stdout.write(`\n@@RESULT@@\n${JSON.stringify(result)}`)
617	    return
618	  }
619	
620	  const names = (values.only ? values.only.split(',') : Object.keys(CORPORA)).filter((name) =>
621	    existsSync(join(options.corpora, CORPORA[name].root)),
622	  )
623	  const report = { generated: new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10), sessions: [], stories: {} }
624	  for (const corpus of names) {

630	    const list = report.sessions.find((x) => x.corpus === corpus && x.variant === 'caliper')?.list ?? []
631	    const real = realStories(rootDir, options.limit)

636	      generated.push(...synthetic)

645	        for (const variant of variants) {

The sampled antd stories dropped from 84 to 67 when the generator stopped importing a file's default export under another component's name; before that, 13 of the 14 "missing" antd props were `Wrapper` compared against `useNotification`.

**Why the degraded rate fell from 42.1% / 27.4% to 4.8% / 4.0%.** The earlier numbers are right for their commit: this harness run against `e31ccb27` (main through #155) gives 42.1% (797 of 1892) for shadcn and 27.4% (68 of 248) for antd, with 13,244 props on shadcn, as recorded below. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A/B speed and memory of this checkout (or a branch) against origin/main, for when a change touches the resolver.

Builds both in release mode, then times `extract --json` over Mantine and Chakra (source directory only, no
dependencies, fetched once into .corpora/) with the two builds interleaved and alternating which goes first, and prints
the median wall time and peak RSS of each side. Calibrated on CI runners and a laptop: with nothing changed, the ratio
stays within 1.04 for time and 1.12 for memory, so more than 1.10x in time or 1.20x in memory is worth a look. Nothing
enforces that.

Usage: scripts/bench.py [BRANCH] [--runs N] [--corpus NAME]...   (BRANCH defaults to this checkout, uncommitted work included)
"""
import argparse
import os
import shutil
import statistics
import subprocess
import tempfile

import corpora
from corpora import ROOT, run_once


def git(*args):
    return subprocess.run(['git', *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()


def build(manifest_dir, target_dir, destination):
    subprocess.run(['cargo', 'build', '--release', '--locked', '-p', 'caliper-docgen', '--manifest-path',
                    os.path.join(manifest_dir, 'Cargo.toml'), '--target-dir', target_dir], check=True)
    shutil.copy(os.path.join(target_dir, 'release', 'caliper-docgen'), destination)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument('branch', nargs='?')
    parser.add_argument('--runs', type=int, default=9)
    parser.add_argument('--corpus', action='append')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.corpus = args.corpus or ['mantine', 'chakra']
    subprocess.run(['git', 'fetch', '-q', 'origin', 'main'], cwd=ROOT)

Fixed: a top-level `const` initialised with a literal (or an object literal with plain keys) is recorded as the alias `typeof NAME` (`extractor/values.rs`), so `typeof NAME` is the literal and `keyof typeof NAME` the union of the keys (`resolver/evaluate.rs`'s `value_type`, `keys_of`); `keyof` of anything else stays opaque, since an interface's keys need its index signatures and every parent. `union_of` folds `true | false` and `boolean | true` into `boolean`. `export default X as <function type>` over a component the file declares takes that function's one props parameter as the props type (`extractor/asserted.rs`). Tests: `crates/core/tests/const_value_types.rs`, `asserted_props.rs`.

**Not fixed, and why.** `Segmented.options` reads optional because its body declares `options = []` and `ParsedProp::new` makes a prop with a default optional, the react-docgen-typescript convention (`types/output.rs`); Storybook's docgen reads the declared type and reports it required. Changing the convention changes every defaulted prop, so it needs its own decision. `BaseUIComponentProps<"div", S>["onClick"]` is an indexed access on a mapped type over an unbound generic with `infer`, which is the documented type-checker gap.

---

"""
assert marker in s
s=s.replace(marker,entry+marker,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='crates/core/src/types/collected.rs'
s=open(p).read()
old="""    // ── `keyof X` — the union of X's own key names. Fully resolved only when
    // consumed by `Omit`'s key argument (`CollectedTypeAlias::Omit::keys`
    // resolves X as a props chain and reads its field names); standalone usage
    // degrades to `PropType::Opaque` since we don't (yet) have a general
    // type-to-key-names resolver outside the chain machinery."""
new="""    // ── `keyof X` — the union of X's own key names. Fully resolved when
    // consumed by `Omit`'s key argument (`CollectedTypeAlias::Omit::keys`
    // resolves X as a props chain and reads its field names), and standalone
    // when X is `typeof` a `const` object literal; any other standalone use
    // degrades to `PropType::Opaque` since we don't (yet) have a general

assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cat > .changeset/const-value-types.md <<'EOF'
---
cargo/caliper-docgen-core: patch
cargo/caliper-docgen: patch
cargo/caliper-docgen-napi: patch
npm/caliper-docgen: patch
---

Props typed from a constant now carry the value TypeScript gives them: `typeof SHOW_PARENT` over `const SHOW_PARENT = 'SHOW_PARENT'` is `"SHOW_PARENT"`, `keyof typeof Icons` over an object literal is the union of its keys, a union of `true` and `false` is `boolean`, and a component exported as `Masonry as (<T>(props: PropsWithChildren<P<T>>) => Element)` has the props of that function type, `children` included.

# 0017. Version the canonical JSON, and make readers reject a version they don't read

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-24

## Context

The canonical JSON has changed shape under its readers once already: ADR 0009 replaced inline props with ids, and nothing told a reader of the old shape. Three packages parse it (`caliper-docgen-napi`'s types, the Vite plugin, the Storybook addon), and so will other tools, such as an agent server linking `caliper-docgen-core`. Semver on the packages and changesets does not guard the JSON: a reader and the binding can be installed at different releases, and the mismatch surfaces as `undefined is not iterable` somewhere downstream.

## Decision

Every canonical JSON document carries `schemaVersion`, an integer: `ExtractionOutput` (CLI `--json` and `--format canonical`, NAPI `extractAll`, `initializeSession`), `IncrementalUpdate`, and the session index (`initializeSessionIndex`). `SCHEMA_VERSION` in `crates/core/src/types/output.rs` is the one definition. The shape ADR 0009 describes is version 1.

- **Bump** when a reader of the previous version would misread or lose data: a field removed, renamed or retyped, a field's meaning changed, or references and tables restructured.
- **Don't bump** for additions a reader can ignore: a new field, a new `detectedBy` value, a new diagnostic code. Readers must tolerate those.
- **Readers** accept their own version and reject any other with an error naming both versions. Output with no `schemaVersion` predates it and has version 1's shape.
- **Release:** a bump goes out in a changeset marked breaking for the core crate and every package that reads the JSON, so writer and readers move together.

# 0017. Version the canonical JSON, and make readers reject a version they don't read

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-24

## Context

The canonical JSON has changed shape under its readers once already: ADR 0009 replaced inline props with ids, and nothing told a reader of the old shape. Three packages parse it (`caliper-docgen-napi`'s types, the Vite plugin, the Storybook addon), and so will other tools, such as an agent server linking `caliper-docgen-core`. Semver on the packages and changesets does not guard the JSON: a reader and the binding can be installed at different releases, and the mismatch surfaces as `undefined is not iterable` somewhere downstream.

## Decision

Every canonical JSON document carries `schemaVersion`, an integer: `ExtractionOutput` (CLI `--json` and `--format canonical`, NAPI `extractAll`, `initializeSession`), `IncrementalUpdate`, and the session index (`initializeSessionIndex`). `SCHEMA_VERSION` in `crates/core/src/types/output.rs` is the one definition. The shape ADR 0009 describes is version 1.

- **Bump** when a reader of the previous version would misread or lose data: a field removed, renamed or retyped, a field's meaning changed, or references and tables restructured.
- **Don't bump** for additions a reader can ignore: a new field, a new `detectedBy` value, a new diagnostic code. Readers must tolerate those.
- **Readers** accept their own version and reject any other with an error naming both versions. Output with no `schemaVersion` predates it and has version 1's shape.
- **Release:** a bump goes out in a changeset marked breaking for the core crate and every package that reads the JSON, so writer and readers move together.
- `--format rdt`, `--format storybook` and `--format toon` have other tools' shapes and carry no version. The parse cache has its own `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.

## Consequences

- A mismatched install fails at the first read with a message that says what to update, instead of a type error deep in a consumer.
- Every shape change needs a deliberate bump, a changeset and a reader update. That is the point, and it costs a small coordinated release each time.
- An old reader cannot read new output at all, even the parts that didn't change. We accept that over a reader that half-works.
- `ExtractionOutput`'s `Deserialize` rejects a version other than `SCHEMA_VERSION`. Reading older versions would need a migration per version, which nothing needs today.

## Alternatives considered

- **Semver of the package as the contract:** readers and the binding are separate installs, so the package version does not say which shape a document has.
- **A range or a minor version in the document:** none of the three readers can use a "compatible up to" statement, and the "don't bump" rule already covers compatible additions.

# NAPI binding

**Source:** `crates/binding/src/lib.rs`, `crates/binding/build.rs`

This is the only consumer-facing FFI boundary in the workspace: a thin `cdylib` that Node.js (concretely, a Vite plugin) calls into. It owns no extraction logic — every entry point marshals `JsExtractOptions` into `PipelineOptions` and delegates straight to `caliper_docgen_core::pipeline`. Its entire job is getting values across the Rust/JS boundary without ever letting a Rust panic reach the Node process, and without ever handing a caller anything other than a proper JS `Error` on failure.

## NAPI entry points

- `extract_all(options) -> String` — cold, one-shot extraction. Runs inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.
- `create_session(options) -> u32` — allocates a session ID, builds a `WatchSession`, inserts it into `SESSIONS`. Runs **synchronously on the calling (JS) thread** — no `spawn_blocking`.
- `initialize_session(session_id, options) -> String` — looks up or lazily creates the session, then returns `WatchSession::initialize()`: the session's current output, running the cold extraction first if the session has none. The Vite plugin's virtual-module `load` uses it as the snapshot. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `extract_file_incremental(file_path, session_id, options) -> String` — looks up or lazily creates the session, then runs `WatchSession::update_file()`. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `session_docgen_info(session_id, keys) -> String` — the named components of the session's current revision in react-docgen-typescript's `__docgenInfo` shape (`pipeline::rdt::docgen_info`), for the Storybook provider (`packages/storybook`). Reads `WatchSession::current_output` without copying it; a key the session lacks, or any key before `initialize_session`, is left out. On a lazy session (below) it resolves the requested components now and answers the rest from the session's memo. Runs synchronously on the calling thread, with `contain_panic` directly.
- `initialize_session_index(session_id, options) -> String` — like `initialize_session`, but returns only what a host needs to find a component and judge whether its props are complete: `{ components: { key: { filePath, displayName } }, diagnostics }`. The props stay in the session for `session_docgen_info`, so a host that documents one component at a time skips serializing every prop. Looks up or lazily creates the session. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `session_component_answers(session_id, keys) -> String` — `{ key: { docgenInfo, diagnostics } }` for each requested component, each diagnostic with `affects` set to the key; a key the session lacks is left out. A lazy session resolves each requested component now, in parallel, so a host learns whether a component's props may be incomplete from the same call that returns them. With `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` the session asks the warm TypeScript 7.1 checker for the component first and waits up to `semanticWaitMs` (default 150) before taking the structural answer (ADR 0022). Synchronous, with `contain_panic` directly.
- `session_warm_up(session_id, count) -> u32` — resolves `count` components spread evenly over the session's keys, without returning them, so a lazy session holds the dependency declarations and resolver memos components share before the first request; the addon uses it for `warmUp` and `fillAfter`. Returns how many it resolved; an eager session, an unknown session and a count of 0 resolve nothing. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `session_component_keys(session_id) -> Vec<String>` and `session_stats(session_id) -> Option<JsLazyStats>` — the keys `session_docgen_info` answers, and what a lazy session has indexed and resolved (`components`, `resolved`, `dependencyFiles`). Synchronous; empty or `None` for an unknown or uninitialized session, and `session_stats` is `None` for an eager one.
- `ensure_fresh(session_id) -> String` — runs `WatchSession::ensure_fresh()`: stats every file the session read and applies what changed since, for a host without a file watcher. Errors for an unknown session, since it has no options to create one from. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `resolution_config_files(session_id) -> Vec<String>` and `is_resolution_config(session_id, file_path) -> bool` — the configs a watcher adds, and whether a changed path is one. Synchronous; empty or false for an unknown session.
- `close_session(session_id) -> ()` — removes the session from `SESSIONS`. Runs synchronously on the calling thread, like `create_session`.

**Lazy sessions (ADR 0016).** `JsExtractOptions.lazy: true` on `create_session` (or on the auto-vivifying `initialize_session` and `extract_file_incremental`) makes a `WatchSession::lazy`. `initialize_session` then parses and indexes every file and returns an `ExtractionOutput` with no components; `extract_file_incremental` and `ensure_fresh` return an `IncrementalUpdate` with `updatedKeys` and `removedKeys` for the memoized components the change can affect, and no `updatedComponents`. Without `lazy` every entry point behaves as before.

`SESSIONS` is `static SESSIONS: LazyLock<DashMap<u32, Arc<WatchSession>>>` — a single process-wide session table. `initialize_session` and `extract_file_incremental` both tolerate a missing session ID by silently constructing a fresh `WatchSession` from the passed `options` and inserting it (`lib.rs:171-179`, `200-208`) — this is a lazy-recovery path, not an error case, so a caller that races `create_session` against `initialize_session` (or never calls `create_session` at all) still gets a working session rather than an "unknown session ID" error.

## Panic-containment boundary (LOCKED DESIGN DECISION — ADR 0005)

Every entry point wraps its real body in `caliper_docgen_core::panic_guard::contain_panic(label, closure)`. This is not incidental defense — it is a deliberate, documented design decision (`docs/adr/0005-panic-containment-boundary.md`) with a specific and non-obvious shape:

- **The `spawn_blocking`-wrapped entry points** (`extract_all`, `initialize_session`, `extract_file_incremental`, `ensure_fresh`) put `contain_panic` **inside** the `spawn_blocking` closure, not around it. Before ADR 0005, these three were only accidentally panic-safe: `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError` happens to catch an unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing, not because anyone decided panic-safety belonged there. Wrapping in `contain_panic` too makes the guarantee a designed one, converts the panic into a `Diagnostic`-derived `napi::Error` message instead of an opaque `JoinError`, and stops being contingent on tokio's internals never changing.

- `session_component_answers(session_id, keys) -> String` — `{ key: { docgenInfo, diagnostics } }` for each requested component, each diagnostic with `affects` set to the key; a key the session lacks is left out. A lazy session resolves each requested component now, in parallel, so a host learns whether a component's props may be incomplete from the same call that returns them. With `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` the session asks the warm TypeScript 7.1 checker for the component first and waits up to `semanticWaitMs` (default 150) before taking the structural answer (ADR 0022). Synchronous, with `contain_panic` directly.
- `session_warm_up(session_id, count) -> u32` — resolves `count` components spread evenly over the session's keys, without returning them, so a lazy session holds the dependency declarations and resolver memos components share before the first request; the addon uses it for `warmUp` and `fillAfter`. Returns how many it resolved; an eager session, an unknown session and a count of 0 resolve nothing. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `session_component_keys(session_id) -> Vec<String>` and `session_stats(session_id) -> Option<JsLazyStats>` — the keys `session_docgen_info` answers, and what a lazy session has indexed and resolved (`components`, `resolved`, `dependencyFiles`). Synchronous; empty or `None` for an unknown or uninitialized session, and `session_stats` is `None` for an eager one.
- `ensure_fresh(session_id) -> String` — runs `WatchSession::ensure_fresh()`: stats every file the session read and applies what changed since, for a host without a file watcher. Errors for an unknown session, since it has no options to create one from. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `resolution_config_files(session_id) -> Vec<String>` and `is_resolution_config(session_id, file_path) -> bool` — the configs a watcher adds, and whether a changed path is one. Synchronous; empty or false for an unknown session.
- `close_session(session_id) -> ()` — removes the session from `SESSIONS`. Runs synchronously on the calling thread, like `create_session`.

**Lazy sessions (ADR 0016).** `JsExtractOptions.lazy: true` on `create_session` (or on the auto-vivifying `initialize_session` and `extract_file_incremental`) makes a `WatchSession::lazy`. `initialize_session` then parses and indexes every file and returns an `ExtractionOutput` with no components; `extract_file_incremental` and `ensure_fresh` return an `IncrementalUpdate` with `updatedKeys` and `removedKeys` for the memoized components the change can affect, and no `updatedComponents`. Without `lazy` every entry point behaves as before.

python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import re
p='docs/architecture/types-and-output-contract.md'
s=open(p).read()
marker="`exported` says whether the component's module exports it"
note="""`degraded_by` (`degradedBy` in JSON) on a `ParsedProp` lists why part of its type is `Opaque`: the reason kinds of the opaque members (`conditionalType`, `mappedType`, `indexedAccess`, ...), each once, in type order. `ParsedProp::new` derives it from `prop_type` (`PropType::degraded_by`), so it never disagrees with the type, and a prop the resolver evaluated in full has no field (`skip_serializing_if`), so a reader of earlier output ignores it and `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays (ADR 0017). A name left as an unexpanded `Named` reference is not `Opaque` and is not listed: its warning is in `diagnostics`, which name the component and not the prop. TOON writes it as a `degradedBy` column only when some prop has one (`toon.rs`).

"""
assert marker in s
s=s.replace(marker,note+marker,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='docs/architecture/napi-binding.md'
s=open(p).read()
marker="- `session_warm_up(session_id, count) -> u32`"
bullet="- `session_component_toon(session_id, key) -> Option<String>` — one component as TOON (`toon::render_component_slice_toon`): its prop table with each prop's declaring type and, when any prop has one, why its type is partly opaque, its inherited layers with the names of a collapsed layer's props, and the warnings and errors that say its props may be incomplete. For an in-process host (an agent) that answers a question about one component and has no use for the whole output; TOON is lossy by design (`toon.rs` module doc). `None` for an unknown session or key; a lazy session resolves the component now. Synchronous, with `contain_panic` directly.\n"
assert marker in s
s=s.replace(marker,bullet+marker,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='docs/edge-cases.md'
s=open(p).read()
i=s.index("## Output")
s=s[:i].rstrip()+"\n"
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
tail -5 docs/edge-cases.md | cut -c1-200
cat > .changeset/prop-level-confidence.md <<'EOF'
---
cargo/caliper-docgen-core: minor
cargo/caliper-docgen: minor
cargo/caliper-docgen-napi: minor
npm/caliper-docgen: minor
npm/caliper-docgen-napi: minor
---

A prop now says why its type is partly a guess: the canonical JSON gains `degradedBy` on a prop whose type holds an opaque member, and the TOON output (`--format toon`) lists each prop's declaring type, quotes string literals in single quotes, shows the names a collapsed inherited layer declares, and adds a `degradedBy` column when a prop has one. A host that works in process can ask the session for one component as TOON with `sessionComponentToon(sessionId, key)` instead of rendering a whole project.
EOF
